summary: ## **CENTRAL ELECTRICITY REGULATORY COMMISSION NEW DELHI** ## **Petition No. 423/MP/2025** ## **Coram:** **Shri Jishnu Barua, Chairperson Shri Ramesh Babu V. Member Shri Harish Dudani, Member Shri Ravinder Singh Dhillon, Member** **Date of Order: 10[th] March, 2026** ## **In the matter of** Petition under Section 79(1)(f) of the Electricity Act, 2003 seeking recovery of illegally deducted trading margin amounts from monthly tariff payment by PTC India Limited. ## **And In the matter of** ## **Everest Power Private Limited,** Hall A, 1[st] floor, Plot No. 143-144, Udyog Vihar, Phase IV, Gurgaon, Haryana – 122002 **Petitioner** ## **VERSUS** **PTC India Limited,** 2[nd] Floor, NBCC Tower, 15, Bhikaji Cama Place, New Delhi- 110066 ** Respondent** **Parties Present:** Shri Anurag Kulharia, Advocate, EPPL Shri Ravi Kishore, Advocate, PTCIL ## **ORDER** The present Petition has been filed by the Petitioner, Everest Power Private Limited (EPPL), seeking the following reliefs: _“ (i) Admit the present Petition;_ _(ii) Direct the Respondent PTC to release illegally deducted trading margin amounts from the Monthly Energy Bills raised by the petitioner along with surcharge thereon amounting to Rs.17,64,34,240/- (Rupees Seventeen Crore Sixty-Four Lakhs Thirty-Four Thousand Two Hundred and Forty only)_ Order in Petition No. 423/MP/2025 Page 1 _(iii) Direct the Respondent PTC to immediately cease nay further deductions from the petitioner’s invoices;_ _(iv) Pass any other Order as this Commission may deem fit and proper in the present facts and circumstances.”_ 2. The present matter was admitted on 24.6.2025, and notice was issued to the Respondent. The Commission directed the Respondent to file its reply, if any, and the Petitioner to file its rejoinder, if any. The Petitioner was further directed to submit, on an affidavit, the details of the Letter of Credit provided by the Respondent to the Petitioner and the details of all trading margin-related bills. The matter was again heard on 14.10.2025, wherein it was adjourned as per the Petitioner’s letter of adjournment dated 13.10.2025; however, the Commission directed the parties to ensure completion of pleadings within three weeks. 3. During the hearing on 3.3.2026, the learned counsel for the Petitioner mentioned the matter and sought permission to withdraw the present Petition on the ground that the issue has been mutually resolved between the parties and the grievance in the matter no longer survives. Learned counsel for the Respondent also submitted that the issue has been settled between the parties. 4. Considering the submissions made by the learned counsels for the parties, the Petitioner is permitted to withdraw the present Petition. 5. Accordingly, Petition No. 423/MP/2025 is disposed of, as withdrawn. Sd/sd/sd/sd/- **(Ravinder Singh Dhillon) (Harish Dudani) (Ramesh Babu V.) (Jishnu Barua) Member Member Member Chairperson** Order in Petition No. 423/MP/2025 Page 2 CERC Website S. No. 172/2026
title: Petition under Section 79(1)(f) of the Electricity Act, 2003 seeking recovery of illegally deducted trading margin amounts from monthly tariff payment by PTC India Limited. Everest Power Private Limited
